1: //! # pathland-view-native
2: //!
3: //! Native (non-WASM) projection of the Pathland flat world, exposed over both a
4: //! Rust API and a C ABI for foreign host languages (Swift / Java / C# / …).
5: //!
6: //! This is the **cross-language, zero-copy** path: a host links this crate as a
7: //! native library (or a `cdylib` and its `pathland_native_*` C functions), drives
8: //! the retained tree with the flat `builder`/`engine` operations, and reads
9: //! opcodes from the **shared-memory ring in place** — no serialization, no batch,
10: //! no WASM.
11: //!
12: //! The surface is the flat `builder`/`engine` world over a native shared-memory
13: //! transport.
14: 
15: use std::collections::{BTreeMap, HashMap};
16: 
17: use pathland_engine::{Engine, SignalId, SignalValue};
18: use pathland_core::{component_type, property_id, MemoryLayout};
19: use pathland_core_transport::{
20:     DriverTransport, FrameSource, OpcodeBatch, RingTransport, TransportError,
21: };
22: use pathland_view::{component_type_id, Node};
23: 
24: mod capi;
25: 
26: /// A flat node in the host's retained tree (id → node).
27: #[derive(Clone)]
28: pub struct FlatNode {
29:     pub id: u32,
30:     pub view_component: pathland_view::Component,
31:     pub properties: BTreeMap<u16, u32>,
32:     /// A signal the node's text is bound to (overrides the component text).
33:     pub text_binding: Option<SignalId>,
34:     /// Property signals (propertyId → signal), overriding static properties.
35:     pub property_bindings: BTreeMap<u16, SignalId>,
36:     pub parent: Option<u32>,
37:     pub children: Vec<u32>,
38: }
39: 
40: /// The native host: owns the retained tree, the diff engine, and the shared
41: /// zero-copy ring.
42: pub struct NativeHost {
43:     nodes: HashMap<u32, FlatNode>,
44:     engine: Engine,
45:     ring: RingTransport,
46: }
47: 
48: /// Safe, checked operations returning `()` (used by the C shim).
49: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
50: pub enum HostError {
51:     /// The operation referenced a missing node.
52:     NotFound,
53: }
54: 
55: impl NativeHost {
56:     /// Create a host with a fresh shared ring (default layout).
57:     pub fn new() -> Self {
58:         Self {
59:             nodes: HashMap::new(),
60:             engine: Engine::new(),
61:             ring: RingTransport::new(),
62:         }
63:     }
64: 
65:     /// Create a host over a caller-provided ring buffer + layout.
66:     pub fn with_buffer(mem: Vec<u8>, layout: MemoryLayout) -> Self {
67:         Self {
68:             nodes: HashMap::new(),
69:             engine: Engine::new(),
70:             ring: RingTransport::with_buffer(mem, layout),
71:         }
72:     }
73: 
74:     /// Create (or reset) a node with a host-supplied stable id.
75:     pub fn create_node(&mut self, id: u32, component: pathland_view::Component) {
76:         let entry = self.nodes.entry(id).or_insert(FlatNode {
77:             id,
78:             view_component: component.clone(),
79:             properties: BTreeMap::new(),
80:             text_binding: None,
81:             property_bindings: BTreeMap::new(),
82:             parent: None,
83:             children: Vec::new(),
84:         });
85:         entry.view_component = component;
86:         entry.properties.clear();
87:         entry.text_binding = None;
88:         entry.property_bindings.clear();
89:     }
90: 
91:     /// Insert `child` into `parent` at `index` (u32::MAX appends).
92:     pub fn insert_child(&mut self, parent: u32, child: u32, index: u32) {
93:         if let Some(p) = self.nodes.get_mut(&parent) {
94:             let idx = if index == u32::MAX {
95:                 p.children.len()
96:             } else {
97:                 (index as usize).min(p.children.len())
98:             };
99:             if !p.children.contains(&child) {
100:                 p.children.insert(idx, child);
101:             }
102:         }
103:         if let Some(c) = self.nodes.get_mut(&child) {
104:             c.parent = Some(parent);
105:         }
106:     }
107: 
108:     /// Remove `child` from `parent`.
109:     pub fn remove_child(&mut self, parent: u32, child: u32) {
110:         if let Some(p) = self.nodes.get_mut(&parent) {
111:             p.children.retain(|c| *c != child);
112:         }
113:         if let Some(c) = self.nodes.get_mut(&child) {
114:             c.parent = None;
115:         }
116:     }
117: 
118:     /// Set a node's text content.
119:     pub fn set_text(&mut self, id: u32, text: &str) {
120:         if let Some(node) = self.nodes.get_mut(&id) {
121:             match &mut node.view_component {
122:                 pathland_view::Component::Text { text: t } => *t = text.into(),
123:                 pathland_view::Component::Button { label } => *label = text.into(),
124:                 _ => {}
125:             }
126:         }
127:     }
128: 
129:     /// Set a constraint/style property (raw value bits; valueType derived from
130:     /// the property id).
131:     pub fn set_property(&mut self, id: u32, prop: u16, value: u32) {
132:         if let Some(node) = self.nodes.get_mut(&id) {
133:             node.properties.insert(prop, value);
134:         }
135:     }
136: 
137:     /// Set a float property (stores `f32` bit pattern).
138:     pub fn set_property_f32(&mut self, id: u32, prop: u16, value: f32) {
139:         self.set_property(id, prop, value.to_bits());
140:     }
141: 
142:     /// Bind a node's text to a signal (the signal's `Str` value wins over any
143:     /// static text). Returns `true` if the node exists.
144:     pub fn bind_text(&mut self, id: u32, signal: SignalId) -> bool {
145:         if let Some(node) = self.nodes.get_mut(&id) {
146:             node.text_binding = Some(signal);
147:             true
148:         } else {
149:             false
150:         }
151:     }
152: 
153:     /// Bind a node's property to a signal. Returns `true` if the node exists.
154:     pub fn bind_property(&mut self, id: u32, prop: u16, signal: SignalId) -> bool {
155:         if let Some(node) = self.nodes.get_mut(&id) {
156:             node.property_bindings.insert(prop, signal);
157:             true
158:         } else {
159:             false
160:         }
161:     }
162: 
163:     /// Create a new signal with an initial value.
164:     pub fn create_signal(&mut self, value: SignalValue) -> SignalId {
165:         self.engine.create_signal(value)
166:     }
167: 
168:     /// Read a signal's current value.
169:     pub fn get_signal(&self, id: SignalId) -> Option<SignalValue> {
170:         self.engine.get_signal(id).cloned()
171:     }
172: 
173:     /// Replace a signal's value, re-emitting only the nodes that depend on it.
174:     ///
175:     /// Writes `SET_PROPERTY` / `SET_TEXT` deltas into the shared ring. Returns
176:     /// `true` if any opcodes were written.
177:     pub fn set_signal(&mut self, id: SignalId, value: SignalValue) -> bool {
178:         let mut guest = self.ring.producer();
179:         guest.begin_frame();
180:         let n = self.engine.set_signal(id, value, &mut guest).unwrap_or(0);
181:         guest.end_frame();
182:         n > 0
183:     }
184: 
185:     /// Emit the retained tree as opcodes into the shared ring.
186:     ///
187:     /// Returns `true` if a frame was written (i.e. the tree is non-empty).
188:     pub fn emit(&mut self) -> bool {
189:         let root = self.root_id().and_then(|r| self.materialize(r));
190:         if let Some(root) = root {
191:             let mut guest = self.ring.producer();
192:             guest.begin_frame();
193:             let _ = self.engine.emit(&root, &mut guest);
194:             guest.end_frame();
195:             true
196:         } else {
197:             false
198:         }
199:     }
200: 
201:     /// The ring's linear-memory buffer (for embedding / FFI).
202:     pub fn ring_buffer(&self) -> &[u8] {
203:         self.ring.buffer()
204:     }
205: 
206:     /// Consume the ring transport (for hosts that read frames via `FrameSource`).
207:     pub fn take_ring(self) -> RingTransport {
208:         self.ring
209:     }
210: 
211:     /// The ring memory layout (region geometry).
212:     pub fn layout(&self) -> MemoryLayout {
213:         *self.layout_ref()
214:     }
215: 
216:     fn layout_ref(&self) -> &MemoryLayout {
217:         self.ring.layout()
218:     }
219: 
220:     /// The single node without a parent (the root).
221:     pub fn root_id(&self) -> Option<u32> {
222:         self.nodes.values().find(|n| n.parent.is_none()).map(|n| n.id)
223:     }
224: 
225:     /// Materialize a `pathland_view::Node` subtree rooted at `id`.
226:     fn materialize(&self, id: u32) -> Option<Node> {
227:         let flat = self.nodes.get(&id)?.clone();
228:         let mut node = Node::from_component(&flat.view_component);
229:         node.id = flat.id;
230:         node.properties = flat.properties.clone();
231:         node.text_binding = flat.text_binding;
232:         node.property_bindings = flat.property_bindings.clone();
233:         for child_id in &flat.children {
234:             if let Some(child) = self.materialize(*child_id) {
235:                 node.children.push(child);
236:             }
237:         }
238:         Some(node)
239:     }
240: }
241: 
242: impl Default for NativeHost {
243:     fn default() -> Self {
244:         Self::new()
245:     }
246: }
247: 
248: /// The host is a `FrameSource` over its shared ring: a renderer drains the
249: /// guest→host frames the engine produced.
250: impl FrameSource for NativeHost {
251:     fn next_frame(&mut self) -> Result<Option<OpcodeBatch<'_>>, TransportError> {
252:         self.ring.next_frame()
253:     }
254: }
255: 
256: /// The host can also write raw inputs (host → guest) into its event ring.
257: impl DriverTransport for NativeHost {
258:     fn send_input(&mut self, event: &pathland_core::Event) -> Result<(), TransportError> {
259:         self.ring.send_input(event)
260:     }
261: }
262: 
263: impl NativeHost {
264:     /// Drain raw-input events written by a renderer into the host → guest event
265:     /// ring (guest side). The application polls this to receive inputs.
266:     pub fn drain_events(&mut self) -> Vec<pathland_core::Event> {
267:         self.ring.drain_events()
268:     }
269: }
270: 
271: /// Map a raw u32 component id (C ABI) to a `pathland_view::Component`.
272: ///
273: /// Mirrors the `component` variant values: hstack=1, vstack=2, text=3,
274: /// button=4, spacer=8.
275: pub fn component_from_id(id: u32) -> Option<pathland_view::Component> {
276:     match id {
277:         x if x == component_type::HSTACK as u32 => Some(pathland_view::Component::HStack),
278:         x if x == component_type::VSTACK as u32 => Some(pathland_view::Component::VStack),
279:         x if x == component_type::TEXT as u32 => {
280:             Some(pathland_view::Component::Text { text: String::new() })
281:         }
282:         x if x == component_type::BUTTON as u32 => {
283:             Some(pathland_view::Component::Button { label: String::new() })
284:         }
285:         x if x == component_type::SPACER as u32 => Some(pathland_view::Component::Spacer),
286:         _ => None,
287:     }
288: }
289: 
290: /// Map a component to its raw u32 id (C ABI).
291: pub fn component_id(component: &pathland_view::Component) -> u32 {
292:     component_type_id(component) as u32
293: }
294: 
295: /// Map a raw u32 property id (C ABI) to a protocol property id and derive its
296: /// value type. `(property_id, is_color)`.
297: pub fn property_value_type(prop: u32) -> (u16, u8) {
298:     let pid = prop as u16;
299:     let vt = if matches!(
300:         pid,
301:         property_id::COLOR | property_id::BACKGROUND_COLOR | property_id::BORDER_COLOR
302:     ) {
303:         pathland_core::value_type::COLOR
304:     } else if pid == property_id::EVENT_LISTENERS {
305:         pathland_core::value_type::U32
306:     } else {
307:         pathland_core::value_type::F32
308:     };
309:     (pid, vt)
310: }
311:

313: mod tests {
314:     use super::*;
315:     use pathland_core::Event;
316: 
317:     #[test]
318:     fn native_host_round_trips_events_via_ring() {
319:         // The host (application) drains raw inputs written by a renderer into
320:         // the host → guest event ring, proving the generic opcode-engine path.

322:

324:             &mut host,

326:         )

329:         assert_eq!(

1: # Pathland Protocol
2: 
3: > A cross-platform, cross-language UI protocol inspired by SwiftUI
4: 
5: ## Overview
6: 
7: Pathland is a **protocol-first** UI framework for **retained-mode UI** with
8: multiple renderer backends. It's inspired by SwiftUI's declarative syntax, but
9: designed to be **language-agnostic** and **platform-agnostic**.
10: 
11: As of August 2026 the core is a **Rust opcode engine**. It emits the
12: application's **declarative view structure** — VStack, HStack, Text, spacing,
13: padding, alignment — as a fixed **16-byte opcode ring buffer** into shared
14: linear memory. Each platform's renderer maps the opcode stream onto that
15: platform's **native elements** (GTK4 widgets on desktop, DOM elements in the
16: browser, HTML server-side) and those native elements lay themselves out.
17: 
18: On desktop the engine runs **natively**: other languages drive it through the
19: flat **native C ABI** (`pathland-view-native`) over a zero-copy shared ring and render
20: through the shared GTK renderer (`pathland-render-gtk`).
21: 
22: **The engine does not compute layout and does not emit rects.** It describes
23: *what* the UI is, never *where* it is. Emission is **diff-based and reactive**:
24: signals in the application ensure only changed nodes emit opcodes, so an
25: unchanged tree emits zero opcodes.
26: 
27: ## The Three Elements
28: 
29: Pathland is composed of three elements. They are the vocabulary the whole
30: project speaks, so they are settled and used consistently:
31: 
32: ```
33: ┌────────────────────┐        ┌─────────────────────┐
34: │ 1. Retained UI     │        │ 3. Renderer         │
35: │ the app's UI tree  │────┐   │ maps opcodes onto   │
36: │ (any language,     │    │   │ native elements +   │
37: │  any platform)     │    │   │ event reporting     │
38: └────────────────────┘    │   └───────────▲─────────┘
39:                          │                │
40: ┌────────────────────┐    │                │
41: │ 2. Opcode engine   │◄───┘                │
42: │ diffs + emits      │─────────────────────┘
43: └────────────────────┘
44: ```
45: 
46: 1. **Retained UI** — the application's canonical retained UI tree. It is the
47:    single source of truth, owned by the application. It can be authored in
48:    **any language on any platform**: Rust, Java, Swift, C#, C, TypeScript —
49:    desktop, mobile, or embedded — through a generated DSL or the flat native C
50:    ABI.
51: 2. **Opcode engine** — walks the retained tree, diffs it, and emits fixed
52:    **16-byte opcodes** (the producer). Emission is reactive: only changed nodes
53:    emit, so an unchanged tree emits zero opcodes. The engine is
54:    language-independent — the same opcode stream serves every renderer.
55: 3. **Renderer** — consumes the opcode stream and maps it onto that platform's
56:    **native elements**, and reports raw inputs back as events. It is a pure
57:    function of the opcode stream (stateless) and never retains application
58:    state. *"Host" and "driver" are roles a renderer plays: it runs inside a
59:    host and is pumped by a driver — they are not separate elements.* The same
60:    opcode stream targets **different UI systems**: a GTK4 renderer on desktop,
61:    an AppKit/SwiftUI renderer on macOS, a WinUI renderer on Windows, an LVGL
62:    renderer on embedded, a DOM renderer in the browser.
63: 
64: The opcodes are carried from the engine to the renderer by a transport (a
65: zero-copy shared-memory ring on desktop/native, a serialized network batch for
66: remote/browser); transport is an implementation detail, not a fourth element.
67: 
68: ## Core Principles
69: 
70: - **Protocol-first**: standardized, open protocol for UI components, events, and raw inputs
71: - **16-byte opcodes**: every instruction is a fixed 16 bytes — cache-line aligned, deterministic, linear decode
72: - **Declarative, not positioned**: the engine emits structure + constraint properties (spacing, padding, alignment); native renderers compute positions
73: - **Native elements everywhere**: GTK4 widgets, DOM elements, HTML — never a generic canvas unless a platform has no native equivalent
74: - **Reactive emission**: only the nodes that changed emit opcodes; steady state emits zero
75: - **Command-based**: UI updates are tree mutations (CREATE_NODE, DELETE_NODE, INSERT_CHILD, MOVE_CHILD, …), never serialized trees
76: - **Stateless renderers**: renderers are pure functions of the opcode stream; they retain only their own rendered output, never application state
77: - **Zero-copy**: ring and arena are plain regions of shared linear memory
78: - **Single-producer / single-consumer**: guest engine produces; host renderer consumes
79: - **Catalog-driven DSL**: the ergonomic SwiftUI-like DSL in any language is generated from a single YAML catalog (`lib/ui/`), not hand-written
80: 
81: ## Documentation
82: 
83: ### Specification
84: 
85: - [Opcode Protocol](./spec/OPCODE.md) — **Primary specification** — fixed 16-byte opcodes, ring buffer, arena, reactive emission, design tokens
86: - [Conformance Test Vectors](./spec/CONFORMANCE.md) — golden byte arrays for validating implementations
87: 
88: ## Rust Workspace
89: 
90: The implementation is under [`lib/rust/`](./lib/rust/):
91: 
92: | Crate | Element | Responsibility |
93: |-------|---------|----------------|
94: | `pathland-view` | Retained UI | SwiftUI-style view DSL: VStack/HStack/Text/Button + chainable modifiers (`no_std`) |
95: | `pathland-core` | Opcode engine | Retained tree types (`Node`/`Component`) + diff-based reactive emitter + reactive **signals** + 16-byte opcode, ring buffer, bump arena (`no_std`, zero-alloc steady state) |
96: | `pathland-core-transport` | Opcode engine | Transport: shared-memory ring + network batch encode/decode + batching policy (`std`) |
97: | `pathland-render-gtk` | Renderer | GTK4 renderer (rlib + cdylib): opcode frames → native GTK widgets, incrementally |
98: | `pathland-view-native` | Retained UI projection | Native C-ABI shim + `NativeHost`: flat world over a zero-copy shared ring (Swift/Java/C#…) |
99: | `pathland-codegen` | Tool | DSL code generator: parses `lib/ui/components.yaml`, asserts ids, emits the Java DSL |
100: | `pathland-render-gtk-demo` | Demo | Rust GTK4 demo: authors the DSL, renders through `pathland-render-gtk` (no GTK APIs) |
101: 
102: The DSL catalog lives in [`lib/ui/components.yaml`](./lib/ui/components.yaml);
103: regenerate the Java DSL with `./generate.sh`.
104: 
105: ### Run tests
106: 
107: ```bash
108: cd lib/rust
109: cargo test
110: ```
111: 
112: ### Run the demos (native, zero-copy shared ring + GTK renderer)
113: 
114: ```bash
115: # Rust demo
116: cd lib/rust && PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH" cargo run -p pathland-render-gtk-demo
117: 
118: # Java demo (JNA over pathland-view-native + pathland-render-gtk)
119: PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH" cargo build -p pathland-view-native -p pathland-render-gtk
120: cd lib/java/pathland-demo && mvn -q -Dpathland.rust.target=<lib/rust/target/debug> compile exec:java
121: ```
122: 
123: On macOS the Java demo must run GTK on the main thread:
124: `MAVEN_OPTS="-XstartOnFirstThread"`.
125: 
126: ## Components & Properties
127: 
128: Component and property IDs are defined in `pathland-core`'s
129: [`constants.rs`](./lib/rust/crates/pathland-core/src/constants.rs) and
130: documented in [OPCODE.md](./spec/OPCODE.md). Component types include `HSTACK`,
131: `VSTACK`, `TEXT`, `BUTTON`, `SPACER`, and more; stack constraint properties
132: (`SPACING`, `ALIGNMENT`, …) drive native layout, styling modifiers (`PADDING`,
133: `COLOR`, `BACKGROUND_COLOR`, …) decorate any view, and `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT`
134: use `-1` = FILL, `-2` = HUG_CONTENT.
135: 
136: ## Design Tokens
137: 
138: The renderer owns default token values; the application owns overrides.
139: Tokens are identified by dot-separated paths (`color.primary`, `space.2`) and
140: referenced via the `DESIGN_TOKEN` value type or overridden globally with
141: `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN`. See [Design Token System](./spec/OPCODE.md#design-token-system).
142: 
143: ## Roadmap (POC Goals)
144: 
145: See the GitHub issues (#12, #13, #15, #16, #18):
146: 
147: 1. **16-byte opcode engine** — done
148: 2. **Core components & modifiers in Rust** (SwiftUI-like API) — done
149: 3. **Opcode transport layer** (shared memory + network batch + native C-ABI shim) — done
150: 4. **Rust desktop app with GTK4 renderer** (native shared ring) — done
151: 5. **Catalog-driven DSL** (YAML → Java via `pathland-codegen`) — done
152: 6. Quarkus SSR + WebSocket demo — planned (browser/remote projection; would
153:    reintroduce a WASM guest + WIT host path)
154: 
155: ## Versioning
156: 
157: Pathland follows **Semantic Versioning** (Major.Minor.Patch). The wire protocol
158: version is 1 (see [OPCODE.md](./spec/OPCODE.md)).
159: 
160: ## License
161: 
162: Pathland is licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0. See the [LICENSE](LICENSE) file for details.

1: //! Batch wire format: encode/decode opcodes + arena delta into network batches.
2: 
3: use alloc::vec::Vec;
4: use pathland_core::{Event, Frame, Opcode, category, event};
5: 
6: use crate::{BATCH_MAGIC, BATCH_VERSION};
7: 
8: /// Fixed header byte length: magic(4) + version(2) + flags(2) + frameCount(4) + opcodeCount(4).
9: pub const BATCH_HEADER: usize = 16;
10: 
11: /// Errors produced while decoding a network batch.
12: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
13: pub enum BatchError {
14:     /// The batch is shorter than the fixed header.
15:     Truncated,
16:     /// The batch magic does not match `BATCH_MAGIC`.
17:     BadMagic,
18:     /// The batch version is not supported.
19:     BadVersion,
20:     /// The opcode payload is truncated (opcodeCount × 16 exceeds the buffer).
21:     BadOpcodeCount,
22:     /// The arena delta length exceeds the remaining buffer.
23:     BadArenaLen,
24: }
25: 
26: /// A decoded network batch: opcodes plus a mirrored arena, exposed as a
27: /// `pathland_core::Frame` so consumers (`RenderTree::apply_frame`) work
28: /// exactly as with shared-memory frames.
29: pub struct Batch<'a> {
30:     frame: Frame<'a>,
31:     frame_count: u32,
32:     flags: u16,
33: }
34: 
35: impl<'a> core::fmt::Debug for Batch<'a> {
36:     fn fmt(&self, f: &mut core::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> core::fmt::Result {
37:         f.debug_struct("Batch")
38:             .field("frame_count", &self.frame_count)
39:             .field("flags", &self.flags)
40:             .field("len", &self.len())
41:             .finish()
42:     }
43: }
44: 
45: impl<'a> Batch<'a> {
46:     /// The opcodes carried by this batch, in order.
47:     pub fn opcodes(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = Opcode> + '_ {
48:         self.frame.opcodes()
49:     }
50: 
51:     /// Number of opcodes in the batch.
52:     pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
53:         self.frame.len()
54:     }
55: 
56:     pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
57:         self.frame.is_empty()
58:     }
59: 
60:     /// The guest frame count the batch spans.
61:     pub fn frame_count(&self) -> u32 {
62:         self.frame_count
63:     }
64: 
65:     /// Direction flags (see [`crate::direction`]).
66:     pub fn flags(&self) -> u16 {
67:         self.flags
68:     }
69: 
70:     /// View this batch as a `Frame` (the transport seam).
71:     pub fn as_frame(&self) -> &Frame<'a> {
72:         &self.frame
73:     }
74: 
75:     /// Read an arena entry by offset (see `Frame::arena_get`).
76:     pub fn arena_get(&self, offset: u32) -> Result<&'a [u8], pathland_core::ArenaError> {
77:         self.frame.arena_get(offset)
78:     }
79: 
80:     /// Read an arena string by offset.
81:     pub fn arena_str(&self, offset: u32) -> Result<&'a str, pathland_core::ArenaError> {
82:         self.frame.arena_str(offset)
83:     }
84: }
85: 
86: /// Serialize one batch from opcodes + an arena delta (bytes appended since the
87: /// previous batch). Stateless; see [`BatchEncoder`] for cursor tracking.
88: pub fn encode_batch(
89:     frame_count: u32,
90:     flags: u16,
91:     opcodes: &[Opcode],
92:     arena_delta: &[u8],
93: ) -> Vec<u8> {
94:     let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(BATCH_HEADER + opcodes.len() * Opcode::SIZE + arena_delta.len() + 4);
95:     out.extend_from_slice(&BATCH_MAGIC.to_le_bytes());
96:     out.extend_from_slice(&BATCH_VERSION.to_le_bytes());
97:     out.extend_from_slice(&flags.to_le_bytes());
98:     out.extend_from_slice(&frame_count.to_le_bytes());
99:     out.extend_from_slice(&(opcodes.len() as u32).to_le_bytes());
100:     for op in opcodes {
101:         out.extend_from_slice(&op.to_bytes());
102:     }
103:     out.extend_from_slice(&(arena_delta.len() as u32).to_le_bytes());
104:     out.extend_from_slice(arena_delta);
105:     out
106: }
107: 
108: /// Fields parsed from a batch header + payload regions.
109: struct ParsedBatch<'a> {
110:     flags: u16,
111:     frame_count: u32,
112:     opcodes: &'a [u8],
113:     arena_delta: &'a [u8],
114: }
115: 
116: /// Parse a batch header, returning flags, frame count, opcode bytes and arena delta.
117: fn parse(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<ParsedBatch<'_>, BatchError> {
118:     if bytes.len() < BATCH_HEADER {
119:         return Err(BatchError::Truncated);
120:     }
121:     let magic = u32::from_le_bytes(bytes[0..4].try_into().unwrap());
122:     if magic != BATCH_MAGIC {
123:         return Err(BatchError::BadMagic);
124:     }
125:     let version = u16::from_le_bytes(bytes[4..6].try_into().unwrap());
126:     if version != BATCH_VERSION {
127:         return Err(BatchError::BadVersion);
128:     }
129:     let flags = u16::from_le_bytes(bytes[6..8].try_into().unwrap());
130:     let frame_count = u32::from_le_bytes(bytes[8..12].try_into().unwrap());
131:     let opcode_count = u32::from_le_bytes(bytes[12..16].try_into().unwrap()) as usize;
132: 
133:     let opcodes_bytes = opcode_count
134:         .checked_mul(Opcode::SIZE)
135:         .ok_or(BatchError::BadOpcodeCount)?;
136:     let opcodes_start = BATCH_HEADER;
137:     let opcodes_end = opcodes_start
138:         .checked_add(opcodes_bytes)
139:         .ok_or(BatchError::BadOpcodeCount)?;
140:     if opcodes_end > bytes.len() {
141:         return Err(BatchError::BadOpcodeCount);
142:     }
143:     let arena_len_pos = opcodes_end;
144:     if arena_len_pos + 4 > bytes.len() {
145:         return Err(BatchError::BadArenaLen);
146:     }
147:     let arena_len = u32::from_le_bytes(bytes[arena_len_pos..arena_len_pos + 4].try_into().unwrap())
148:         as usize;
149:     let arena_start = arena_len_pos + 4;
150:     let arena_end = arena_start
151:         .checked_add(arena_len)
152:         .ok_or(BatchError::BadArenaLen)?;
153:     if arena_end > bytes.len() {
154:         return Err(BatchError::BadArenaLen);
155:     }
156: 
157:     Ok(ParsedBatch {
158:         flags,
159:         frame_count,
160:         opcodes: &bytes[opcodes_start..opcodes_end],
161:         arena_delta: &bytes[arena_start..arena_end],
162:     })
163: }
164: 
165: /// A streamed network-batch encoder.
166: ///
167: /// Tracks the last arena length so successive batches carry only the bytes
168: /// appended to the bump arena since the previous batch. If the arena is reset
169: /// (shrank — see `META::RESET`), the full used arena is sent and tracking
170: /// restarts.
171: #[derive(Debug, Default)]
172: pub struct BatchEncoder {
173:     last_arena_len: usize,
174: }
175: 
176: impl BatchEncoder {
177:     /// Create a fresh encoder (no arena bytes sent yet).
178:     pub fn new() -> Self {
179:         Self { last_arena_len: 0 }
180:     }
181: 
182:     /// Encode a frame's opcodes plus the arena bytes appended since the last
183:     /// call. `arena_used` is the arena region's used portion (`[0..cursor)`).
184:     ///
185:     /// If the frame contains `META::RESET`, arena tracking restarts (the arena
186:     /// cursor returns to 0) and the full used arena is sent.
187:     pub fn encode(&mut self, frame_count: u32, opcodes: &[Opcode], arena_used: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
188:         let reset = opcodes.iter().any(|op| {
189:             op.category() == pathland_core::category::META
190:                 && op.command() == pathland_core::meta::RESET
191:         });
192:         if reset {
193:             self.last_arena_len = 0;
194:         }
195:         let delta = if arena_used.len() >= self.last_arena_len {
196:             &arena_used[self.last_arena_len..]
197:         } else {
198:             // Arena shrank unexpectedly: send the full used arena again.
199:             arena_used
200:         };
201:         let bytes = encode_batch(frame_count, crate::direction::GUEST_TO_HOST, opcodes, delta);
202:         self.last_arena_len = arena_used.len();
203:         bytes
204:     }
205: 
206:     /// The arena length already shipped (diagnostics).
207:     pub fn arena_sent(&self) -> usize {
208:         self.last_arena_len
209:     }
210: }
211: 
212: /// A streamed network-batch decoder.
213: ///
214: /// Maintains a **mirrored arena**: each batch's arena delta is appended, so
215: /// absolute `arenaRef` offsets resolve exactly as in shared memory. When a
216: /// batch contains `META::RESET`, the mirror is cleared before appending.
217: #[derive(Debug, Default)]
218: pub struct BatchDecoder {
219:     arena: Vec<u8>,
220: }
221: 
222: impl BatchDecoder {
223:     /// Create an empty decoder.
224:     pub fn new() -> Self {
225:         Self { arena: Vec::new() }
226:     }
227: 
228:     /// Decode a batch, appending its arena delta to the mirror.
229:     ///
230:     /// The returned `Batch` borrows `bytes` (opcodes) and this decoder (arena);
231:     /// keep both alive while consuming it.
232:     pub fn decode<'a>(&'a mut self, bytes: &'a [u8]) -> Result<Batch<'a>, BatchError> {
233:         let parsed = parse(bytes)?;
234: 
235:         // A META::RESET in the batch clears the renderer; reset the arena mirror
236:         // to match (offsets restart at 0 after a reset).
237:         let opcode_count = parsed.opcodes.len() / Opcode::SIZE;
238:         let reset = (0..opcode_count).any(|i| {
239:             let op = Opcode::from_bytes(parsed.opcodes[i * Opcode::SIZE..(i + 1) * Opcode::SIZE].try_into().unwrap());
240:             op.category() == pathland_core::category::META
241:                 && op.command() == pathland_core::meta::RESET
242:         });
243:         if reset {
244:             self.arena.clear();
245:         }
246:         self.arena.extend_from_slice(parsed.arena_delta);
247: 
248:         let frame = Frame::from_parts(parsed.opcodes, &self.arena, 0, parsed.opcodes.len());
249:         Ok(Batch {
250:             frame,

262: /// Encode raw-input events as a host → guest batch.
263: ///
264: /// Events are `EVENT`-category opcodes; the batch reuses the wire format with
265: /// the `HOST_TO_GUEST` direction flag. `TextChanged` events carry their text in
266: /// the batch's string section (a length-prefixed entry referenced by the
267: /// opcode's `B` offset), so the string section is only empty when there are no
268: /// text events.
269: pub fn encode_events(frame_count: u32, events: &[Event]) -> Vec<u8> {
270:     let mut opcodes = Vec::new();
271:     let mut strings = Vec::new();
272:     for ev in events {
273:         match ev {
274:             Event::TextChanged { target, value } => {
275:                 let offset = strings.len() as u32;
276:                 strings.extend_from_slice(&(value.len() as u32).to_le_bytes());
277:                 strings.extend_from_slice(value.as_bytes());
278:                 opcodes.push(Opcode::new(
279:                     category::EVENT,
280:                     event::TEXT_CHANGED,
281:                     0,
282:                     *target,
283:                     offset,
284:                     0,
285:                 ));
286:             }
287:             other => opcodes.push(other.encode()),
288:         }
289:     }
290:     encode_batch(frame_count, crate::direction::HOST_TO_GUEST, &opcodes, &strings)
291: }

293: /// Decode a host → guest event batch, returning `(frame_count, events)`.
294: ///
295: /// Unknown or malformed event opcodes are skipped. `TextChanged` opcodes
296: /// resolve their text from the batch's string section.
297: pub fn decode_events(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<(u32, Vec<Event>), BatchError> {
298:     let mut decoder = BatchDecoder::new();
299:     let batch = decoder.decode(bytes)?;
300:     let events = batch
301:         .opcodes()
302:         .filter_map(|op| {
303:             if op.category() == category::EVENT && op.command() == event::TEXT_CHANGED {
304:                 batch
305:                     .arena_str(op.b())
306:                     .ok()
307:                     .map(|text| Event::TextChanged {
308:                         target: op.a(),
309:                         value: text.to_string(),
310:                     })
311:             } else {
312:                 Event::try_from(op).ok()
313:             }
314:         })
315:         .collect();
316:     Ok((batch.frame_count(), events))
317: }

319: /// Build a self-contained `Frame` view over in-memory opcodes + a string
320: /// section — the **in-process transport seam**.
321: ///
322: /// `slots` is reused as the opcode byte buffer (cleared, then the 16-byte
323: /// opcodes written in), so the returned `Frame` borrows both `slots` and
324: /// `strings` with no serialization. This is how an in-process consumer receives
325: /// the same `Frame` view a ring or network decoder would produce.
326: pub fn frame_from_slices<'a>(
327:     slots: &'a mut Vec<u8>,
328:     strings: &'a [u8],
329:     opcodes: &[Opcode],
330: ) -> Frame<'a> {
331:     slots.clear();
332:     slots.extend(opcodes.iter().flat_map(Opcode::to_bytes));
333:     let bytes: &'a [u8] = slots;
334:     Frame::from_parts(bytes, strings, 0, bytes.len())
335: }

337: /// Encode a **self-contained** frame as a network batch.
338: ///
339: /// `opcodes` is the frame's commands and `strings` its per-frame string
340: /// section: every `SET_TEXT` opcode references its string by a *relative*
341: /// offset into `strings` (not an absolute arena offset). The batch therefore
342: /// decodes with no prior state — no mirrored arena, no delta tracking — which
343: /// is what makes each WebSocket message independent.
344: ///
345: /// This is the network/stream codec. The shared-memory path uses
346: /// [`encode_batch`]/[`BatchEncoder`] instead, whose arena offsets are absolute
347: /// and mirrored on the consumer.
348: pub fn encode_frame(opcodes: &[Opcode], strings: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
349:     encode_batch(0, crate::direction::GUEST_TO_HOST, opcodes, strings)
350: }
351: 
352: /// Decode a self-contained frame batch, returning `(opcodes, strings)`.
353: ///
354: /// Stateless: unlike [`BatchDecoder`], no arena mirror is maintained, because
355: /// the batch carries its own string section and the offsets are relative to it.
356: pub fn decode_frame(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<(Vec<Opcode>, Vec<u8>), BatchError> {
357:     let parsed = parse(bytes)?;
358:     let count = parsed.opcodes.len() / Opcode::SIZE;
359:     let opcodes = (0..count)
360:         .map(|i| {
361:             let start = i * Opcode::SIZE;
362:             Opcode::from_bytes(parsed.opcodes[start..start + Opcode::SIZE].try_into().unwrap())
363:         })
364:         .collect();
365:     Ok((opcodes, parsed.arena_delta.to_vec()))
366: }

2: //!
3: //! Producer side serializes Frames into network batches (opcodes + arena delta);
4: //! the consumer decodes them with `BatchDecoder` (see `crate::batch`) back into
5: //! `Frame` views consumed by `RenderTree::apply_frame`. This is the remote/SSR
6: //! path where producer and consumer do **not** share memory.
7: //!
8: //! The wire format is unchanged from `crate::batch` (magic/version/flags/
9: //! frameCount/opcodeCount/opcodes/arenaDeltaLen/arena).

15: use crate::batch::encode_batch;

17: /// Producer-side network batch encoder.
18: ///
19: /// Buffers opcodes (from Frames) and serializes them into a batch with the
20: /// arena's used-arena slice. Use the `Batcher` helper (`crate::batching`) for a
21: /// time/size flush policy; this type is the bare encoder for explicit flushes.
22: #[derive(Debug, Default)]
23: pub struct NetBatchEncoder {
24:     opcodes: Vec<Opcode>,
25: }
26: 
27: impl NetBatchEncoder {
28:     /// Append a frame's opcodes to the pending batch.
29:     pub fn push_frame(&mut self, frame: &Frame<'_>) {
30:         self.opcodes.extend(frame.opcodes());
31:     }
32: 
33:     /// Append raw opcodes to the pending batch.
34:     pub fn push_opcodes(&mut self, opcodes: &[Opcode]) {
35:         self.opcodes.extend_from_slice(opcodes);
36:     }
37: 
38:     /// Serialize the pending opcodes with a provided used-arena slice, clearing
39:     /// the buffer. `frame_count` is the covering frame counter.
40:     pub fn encode_with_arena(&mut self, frame_count: u32, arena_used: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
41:         let bytes = encode_batch(
42:             frame_count,
43:             crate::direction::GUEST_TO_HOST,
44:             &self.opcodes,
45:             arena_used,
46:         );
47:         self.opcodes.clear();
48:         bytes
49:     }
50: 
51:     /// Whether any opcodes are buffered.
52:     pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
53:         self.opcodes.is_empty()
54:     }
55: 
56:     /// Number of buffered opcodes.
57:     pub fn pending(&self) -> usize {
58:         self.opcodes.len()
59:     }
60: }

1: //! # pathland-core-transport
2: //!
3: //! How Pathland opcodes are transported from the guest engine to host
4: //! renderers. There are two peer backends:
5: //!
6: //! - **Shared memory** (desktop/native/WASM): the ring buffer + arena in
7: //!   `pathland-core` (`Guest`/`Host`). Zero-copy. This crate treats it as
8: //!   the local transport — no duplication.
9: //! - **Network batch** (SSR → browser): opcodes + string data serialized into
10: //!   **batches**.
11: //!
12: //! There are two network codecs, for two different relationships between the
13: //! producer and the consumer:
14: //!
15: //! - **Self-contained frames** ([`encode_frame`] / [`decode_frame`]) — each
16: //!   batch carries its own string section and `SET_TEXT` references strings by
17: //!   a *relative* offset into that section. The consumer needs **no prior
18: //!   state**: every message is independent. This is the streaming codec used
19: //!   for live deltas over WebSocket.
20: //! - **Arena-delta batches** ([`encode_batch`] / [`BatchEncoder`] /
21: //!   [`BatchDecoder`]) — the batch carries only the bytes *appended* to the
22: //!   arena since the previous batch, and `SET_TEXT` references absolute arena
23: //!   offsets. The consumer mirrors the arena so those offsets stay valid. This
24: //!   mirrors the shared-memory arena over a wire and is the ring-compatible
25: //!   codec (kept for a future WASM/embedded guest).
26: //!
27: //! ## Batch wire format (both codecs share the header)
28: //!
29: //! ```text
30: //! magic "PLPL" (u32 LE) | version (u16) | flags (u16) | frameCount (u32)
31: //! | opcodeCount (u32) | opcodes (16 B × opcodeCount) | stringsLen (u32)
32: //! | string bytes (length-prefixed entries: [u32 len][bytes])
33: //! ```
34: //!
35: //! For a self-contained frame the trailing section is that frame's own string
36: //! table; for an arena-delta batch it is the arena bytes appended since the
37: //! last batch.
38: //!
39: //! ## Example (producer)
40: //!
41: //! ```no_run
42: //! use pathland_core_transport::{Batcher, BatchPolicy, BatchEncoder};
43: //! use std::time::Duration;
44: //!
45: //! let policy = BatchPolicy::new(Duration::from_millis(4), 1400);
46: //! let mut batcher = Batcher::new(policy);
47: //! let mut encoder = BatchEncoder::new();
48: //!
49: //! // batcher.push_frame(&frame) accumulates opcodes + arena delta;
50: //! // batcher.flush() -> Option<Vec<u8>> produces the serialized batch.
51: //! ```
52: 
53: #![forbid(unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn)]

65:     decode_events, decode_frame, encode_batch, encode_events, encode_frame, frame_from_slices,
66:     Batch, BatchDecoder, BatchEncoder,

68: pub use batching::{Batcher, BatchPolicy};

I've completed a thorough exploration of the codebase. Before I finalize the plan, I need to resolve several important discrepancies and decisions. Let me summarize what I found, then ask focused questions.

**Key findings:**
1. The current Java DSL (`pathland.*` package) is auto-generated by `lib/rust/crates/pathland-codegen` from `lib/ui/components.yaml`. It drives the Rust engine via the `pathland_native_*` **builder** C ABI (Rust owns the retained tree + diff engine) through JNA, and renders via `pathland-render-gtk`.
2. `pathland_ring_buffer_push(const PathlandOpcode*)` **does not exist** in Rust today. The task describes a *different* integration model: Java owns the retained tree + diff emitter and pushes raw 16-byte opcodes straight into the Rust SPSC ring.
3. The opcode layout in task §2A (`u8 type + u32 target + u16 prop + u64 payload` = 15 bytes) **does not match** the actual wire layout `[Category u8][Command u8][Flags u16][A u32][B u32][C u32]` = 16 bytes, which AGENTS.md marks NON-NEGOTIABLE.
4. `Arena.ofAuto()` / final FFM requires **Java 22+** (JDK 25 is installed; default JDK is 17). `ScopedValue` needs 21+.
5. `pathland-render-html` is a Rust crate; a Quarkus (Java) demo can't call it directly.
6. Quarkus 3.17.6 is already in the local Maven repo (with Jackson, Vert.x-http); WebSocket + Redis extensions are *not* cached and would be downloaded.

questions.question: The task says Java pushes raw opcodes via `pathland_ring_buffer_push(const PathlandOpcode*)` — but that C entry point doesn't exist today. Today the Rust side owns the retained tree + diff engine (the `pathland_native_*` builder). Which integration model should the new hand-written DSL use?

options.label: Raw opcodes into a new minimal Rust ring C ABI (Recommended)
options.description: Java owns the retained tree + diff emitter, emits 16-byte opcodes directly, and pushes them via FFM into a NEW small Rust cdylib (libpathland_core) exposing only the SPSC ring (create/push/frame/read/drain-events/destroy). Matches the task text literally; largest effort.

options.label: Keep existing pathland_native_* builder
options.description: Rust keeps owning the tree/diff; only swap generated DSL for hand-written Java + JNA. Much smaller, but does not implement pathland_ring_buffer_push and keeps JNA (not FFM).

questions.question: Task §2A lists a 15-byte layout (u8 type + u32 target + u16 prop + u64 payload) that doesn't match the real 16-byte wire format. Which should the DSL encode?

options.label: Real 16-byte layout (Recommended)
options.description: [Category u8][Command u8][Flags u16][A u32][B u32][C u32] little-endian, matching pathland-core::Opcode and spec/OPCODE.md (NON-NEGOTIABLE).

options.label: The 15-byte layout from the task
options.description: Use the simplified layout exactly as written in §2A, diverging from the Rust core spec.

questions.question: pathland-render-html is a Rust crate. How should the Java Quarkus demo produce SSR HTML from opcodes?

options.label: Java HTML renderer (Recommended)
options.description: Port pathland-render-html's logic into a zero-dependency Java class (com.pathland.render.html.HtmlRenderer) that consumes the opcodes the DSL already produced. No round-trip through Rust; keeps the 'hand-crafted Java' narrative.

options.label: Expose Rust HtmlRenderer via C ABI
options.description: Add C-ABI functions to call the Rust pathland-render-html over FFM/JNA. More native plumbing, keeps a single renderer implementation.

questions.question: lib/java/pathland-demo (JNA + pathland-render-gtk) depends on the generated `pathland.*` package. After removing codegen, what should happen to it?

options.label: Delete the old demo (Recommended)
options.description: Remove lib/java/pathland-demo entirely; the new pathland-dsl library + pathland-quarkus-demo replace it.

options.label: Migrate it to the new DSL
options.description: Rewrite the GTK demo to use com.pathland.dsl, keeping a desktop Java demo (adds effort; GTK renderer stays Rust via JNA).

questions.question: Task §3 wants StateStore working on Redis / File+SQLite / WASM LocalStorage / ESP32 NVS. Which should be actually implemented vs. defined-and-documented?

options.label: Interface + InMemory/File/SQLite + Redis, doc-only for WASM/ESP32 (Recommended)
options.description: Implement StateStore<T> + SPI, plus InMemory, JSON File, JDBC SQLite, and Redis (Lettuce) backends. Define the WASM LocalStorage and ESP32 NVS contracts + docs only (they can't run on a JVM).

options.label: Interface + InMemory + Redis only
options.description: Minimal: interface + SPI + in-memory and Redis; skip File/SQLite too.

options.label: Everything concrete
options.description: Attempt all four platforms with real code (WASM/ESP32 would be stubbed since they're non-JVM).

questions.question: Final FFM (Arena.ofAuto, MemorySegment, FunctionDescriptor) requires Java 22+. JDK 25 is installed; Quarkus 3.17.6 is cached. What should the modules target?

options.label: Java 22+ on JDK 25, Quarkus 3.17 (Recommended)
options.description: Set maven.compiler.release=22 (or 25); use the installed Temurin 25 and Quarkus 3.17.6 platform. FFM + ScopedValue fully final.

options.label: Java 21 with FFM preview
options.description: Target LTS 21 with --enable-preview for java.lang.foreign; ScopedValue final. More friction (preview flags, no Arena.ofAuto).

# Plan: Native Java DSL + Quarkus SSR/WebSocket Demo

## Locked decisions
- **Integration:** Java owns the retained tree + diff emitter; pushes raw 16-byte opcodes into a **new minimal Rust ring C ABI** (`libpathland_core`) via FFM.
- **Wire format:** the real 16-byte layout `[Category u8][Command u8][Flags u16][A u32][B u32][C u32]` (little-endian), matching `pathland-core::Opcode`.
- **HTML:** Java port of `pathland-render-html` (`com.pathland.render.html.HtmlRenderer`).
- **Old demo:** delete `lib/java/pathland-demo`.
- **State:** `StateStore<T>` + SPI + `InMemoryStateStore` + `RedisStateStore` (Lettuce/Quarkus Redis); WASM/ESP32 documented as contracts only.
- **Toolchain:** Java 22+ on JDK 25 Temurin, Quarkus 3.17.6.

---

## Phase 1 — Purge codegen (cleanup)
1. Delete `lib/rust/crates/pathland-codegen/` (both files).
2. Remove `"crates/pathland-codegen"` from `lib/rust/Cargo.toml` `members`.
3. Delete `generate.sh`.
4. Delete `lib/ui/components.yaml` (+ `lib/ui/`) — codegen was its only consumer.
5. Delete `lib/java/pathland-demo/` entirely.
6. Update `README.md` + `AGENTS.md`: drop codegen/catalog/JNA-GTK references; add the new DSL + Quarkus demo sections.
7. Verify `cd lib/rust && cargo test` still green.

## Phase 2 — New Rust crate `pathland-core-capi` (`libpathland_core` cdylib)
New `lib/rust/crates/pathland-core-capi/` (`[lib] name = "pathland_core", crate-type = ["cdylib","rlib"]`), depending on `pathland-core` + `pathland-core-transport`. Exposes a minimal ring C ABI:
- `pathland_core_create() -> *mut c_void` / `pathland_core_destroy(h)`
- `bool pathland_ring_buffer_push(h, const u8* opcode /*16B*/)` — write one opcode at `writeCursor`, false when full
- `void pathland_core_begin_frame(h)` / `void pathland_core_end_frame(h)` — frame boundaries + `frameCount`
- `const u8* pathland_core_ring_ptr(h)` / `uint64 pathland_core_ring_len(h)` — zero-copy read
- `uint32 pathland_core_drain_events(h, u8* out, uint32 max)` / `void pathland_core_send_event(...)` — host→guest events
- Add the crate to the workspace `members`; add unit tests (push → read back the same 16 bytes).

## Phase 3 — Java DSL library `lib/java/pathland-dsl` (`com.pathland.dsl`)
Zero-dependency (JDK-only) Maven library, `maven.compiler.release=22`. Core API per the task:
- `sealed interface View { PathlandNode render(Environment env); }` with default modifiers: `padding(int)`, `background(Color)`, `color`, `opacity`, `fontSize`, `frame(w,h,alignment)`, `modifier(ViewModifier)`, `buttonStyle(ButtonStyle)`, `onTapGesture(Runnable)`.
- `Environment` — `ScopedValue<ButtonStyle>`-backed; `.buttonStyle(style)` scopes a style down the child tree.
- `ButtonStyle { View makeBody(Configuration config); }` + `record Configuration(View label)`; built-ins `BorderedButtonStyle`, `PlainButtonStyle`.
- `@FunctionalInterface ViewModifier { View body(View content); }`.
- `record Binding<T>(Supplier<T> getter, Consumer<T> setter)` + helpers.
- Leaf primitives `Text`, `Image`, `Color`, `Rectangle`; layout `VStack`/`HStack`/`ZStack` (varargs + `List<View>`); `Button(View label, Runnable)` + `Button(String, Runnable)`; `TextField(String placeholder, Binding<String>)`.
- Protocol constants mirroring `constants.rs` (component/property ids, `FILL=-1`/`HUG_CONTENT=-2`, listener bits, value types).
- Retained tree + emitter: `PathlandNode`, stable id assignment, **diff** (create/delete/insert/remove/move + set_property/set_text) → `Opcode` (16-byte) → `OpcodeSink`.
- `OpcodeSink` abstraction with two implementations:
  - `RingOpcodeSink` — writes opcodes into a reused native `MemorySegment` via FFM `pathland_ring_buffer_push` (zero-copy, no JNI, no per-op heap).
  - `FrameOpcodeSink` — accumulates opcodes + a string section into a **self-contained frame** (relative string offsets) for the Quarkus path.
- FFM bindings: `PathlandCore` using `Linker`/`SymbolLookup`/`FunctionDescriptor`/`Arena.ofAuto()`; `SymbolLookup.libraryLookup("pathland_core", arena)`.
- Codec `com.pathland.dsl.transport`: `FrameEncoder/Decoder` (mirror `encode_frame`/`decode_frame`) and `EventEncoder/Decoder` (mirror `encode_events`/`decode_events`) — the `PLPL` batch header format.

## Phase 4 — Java HTML renderer `com.pathland.render.html`
Pure-function port of `pathland-render-html`'s `HtmlRenderer` (apply opcodes → retained `BTreeMap` node map → HTML with `data-pathland-id`, VStack/HStack/Text/Button/Switch/Checkbox/Slider/TextField/Spacer + borders). No dependencies.

## Phase 5 — Quarkus demo `lib/java/pathland-quarkus-demo`
Quarkus 3.17.6 app (deps: `quarkus-rest`, `quarkus-websockets-next`, `quarkus-redis-client`), depending on `pathland-dsl`:

- `GET /` → SSR via Java `HtmlRenderer`, injects `app.js`.
- `@WebSocket("/ws")` → broadcasts self-contained frames (Java `FrameEncoder`); receives binary `EVENT` batches, decodes via `EventDecoder`, dispatches PointerUp → action / ValueChanged / TextChanged → state.
- `StateStore` wiring: a `RedisStateStore` (active when Redis configured, `InMemoryStateStore` fallback otherwise) persists a sample value, demonstrating the cross-platform abstraction; a `state/README.md` (or Javadoc) documents the File/SQLite/LocalStorage/NVS contracts for the non-JVM targets.
- `static/app.js` — reuse the existing client (hydrates `[data-pathland-id]`, applies `SET_TEXT`/`SET_PROPERTY`, sends EVENT batches).

## Phase 6 — Verification
1. `cd lib/rust && cargo test` (all crates, incl. new capi).
2. `cargo build -p pathland-core-capi` → `libpathland_core.dylib`.
3. `cd lib/java/pathland-dsl && mvn -q test` — round-trip test: view → opcodes → Java HtmlRenderer → expected HTML + a FFM push/read test (skip-if-native-lib-missing).
4. `cd lib/java/pathland-quarkus-demo && mvn -q quarkus:dev` (or `mvn package` + run) — `curl /` returns SSR HTML; WebSocket delta streaming verified manually or via a small client test.

- The Java diff emitter is deliberately simpler than Rust's dependency-graph signal engine: it re-renders + diffs (emitting only deltas), which satisfies "only changed nodes emit" without a full dependency graph — acceptable for the demo and documented as such.
- FFM downcall into `pathland_ring_buffer_push` needs `--enable-native-access=ALL-UNNAMED` (or the library's module) on the JVM; the Quarkus/dev run script will set it.

## Revised module structure (Maven, `org.pathland`)

```
lib/java/                          (Maven multi-module reactor)
├── pom.xml                        parent: shared version, compiler.release=22
├── pathland-dsl/                  org.pathland:pathland-dsl         ← ZERO-dependency (JDK only)
│     com.pathland.dsl             View/Environment/primitives/controls/modifiers/ButtonStyle
│     com.pathland.dsl.signal      Signal/WritableSignal/computed/effect/untracked
│     com.pathland.dsl.emit        PathlandNode/Opcode/Emitter/OpcodeSink
│     com.pathland.dsl.transport   FrameEncoder/Decoder, EventEncoder/Decoder (PLPL codec)
│     com.pathland.dsl.state       StateStore<T> + StateStoreProvider + InMemoryStateStore
│     com.pathland.dsl.native      FFM binding (PathlandCore) + RingOpcodeSink (lazy/optional)
├── pathland-render-html/          org.pathland:pathland-render-html  ← depends on dsl (codec/constants)
│     com.pathland.render.html     HtmlRenderer (pure function of opcodes → HTML)
├── pathland-state-redis/          org.pathland:pathland-state-redis  ← depends on dsl + Lettuce
│     com.pathland.state.redis     RedisStateStore (Lettuce, framework-agnostic)
└── pathland-quarkus-demo/         org.pathland:pathland-quarkus-demo ← depends on dsl, render-html, state-redis
```

**Why this decomposition enables Spring Boot / Desktop / Quarkus equally:**
- `pathland-dsl` and `pathland-render-html` carry **zero framework or client deps** — a Spring Boot app depends on `pathland-dsl` + `pathland-render-html` and renders SSR + WebSocket deltas with no Quarkus anywhere.
- The **native FFM binding is lazy and optional**: `PathlandCore` loads `libpathland_core` on first use via `SymbolLookup.libraryLookup`. Server apps (Spring/Quarkus) never touch the ring and never require the native lib; a desktop app uses the same `pathland-dsl` plus the `RingOpcodeSink` to push opcodes zero-copy.
- **Redis is Lettuce-based** (portable across Spring Boot, Quarkus, plain JVM desktop) in its own module, so the framework-agnostic core never drags a Redis/HTTP dependency. (Drops `quarkus-redis-client`.)
- State is reusable everywhere: `StateStore<T>` + `InMemoryStateStore` ship in the zero-dep `pathland-dsl`; `RedisStateStore` is the optional Redis module; File/SQLite/LocalStorage/NVS remain documented contracts.

The Quarkus demo becomes a thin shell: `@WebSocket` + a `GET /` resource + an `app.js` static asset, all delegating to the libraries.

13: /// A zero-copy SPSC shared-memory ring transport.
14: ///
15: /// Owns the linear-memory buffer (header + ring + arena). Producers and
16: /// consumers are granted short-lived `Guest`/`Host` views over the same buffer
17: /// via the borrowed methods, so opcodes flow in place with no copies.

69: 
70: - **Protocol-first**: standardized, open protocol for UI components, events, and raw inputs
71: - **16-byte opcodes**: every instruction is a fixed 16 bytes — cache-line aligned, deterministic, linear decode

75: - **Command-based**: UI updates are tree mutations (CREATE_NODE, DELETE_NODE, INSERT_CHILD, MOVE_CHILD, …), never serialized trees
76: - **Stateless renderers**: renderers are pure functions of the opcode stream; they retain only their own rendered output, never application state
77: - **Zero-copy**: ring and arena are plain regions of shared linear memory
78: - **Single-producer / single-consumer**: guest engine produces; host renderer consumes

### Native Java DSL (`com.pathland.view`, in `lib/java/pathland-view`)

The **hand-written, zero-dependency Java 22+ DSL** (no codegen). It is the
SwiftUI-like authoring surface shared by desktop, Spring Boot, and Quarkus
apps. Components and modifiers:

- `View` is a **sealed interface** — `Text`/`Image`/`Color`/`Rectangle`,
  `VStack`/`HStack`/`ZStack`, `Spacer`, `Button(View label, Runnable)` +
  `Button(String, Runnable)`, `TextField(placeholder, WritableSignal<String>)`.
- **Constructor props** (structural/layout: `alignment`, `spacing`) are
  constructor args, never chainable; **modifiers** (`padding`, `color`,
  `background`, `fontSize`, `fontWeight`, `frame`, `opacity`, `border`,
  `visible`, …) chain on any view. No standalone width/height — use the
  compound `frame(width, height, alignment)` modifier. Typed enums
  (`Alignment`/`TextAlignment`/`FontWeight`/`Truncation`), not raw ints.
- **Environment scoping via `ScopedValue`** (Java 21+): `.buttonStyle(ButtonStyle)`
  injects a style down the whole child tree; `ButtonStyle.makeBody(Configuration)`
  with built-in `PlainButtonStyle` / `BorderedButtonStyle`. Custom wrappers via
  `ViewModifier.body(View)`.
- **Reactivity (Angular parity)** in `com.pathland.view.signal`:
  `Signals.signal/computed/effect/untracked` — lazy+memoized computeds,
  glitch-free synchronous flush, equality suppression, error caching, write
  discipline (`allowWrites()`), circular-dependency detection.
- **Fine-grained emitter** (`com.pathland.view.emit`): mounts a view tree once,
  assigns stable ids, and registers a **node-level binding effect** per reactive
  text/property — a signal change re-emits only that node's `SET_TEXT` /
  `SET_PROPERTY` (unchanged signals emit zero opcodes). Sinks: `FrameOpcodeSink`
  (self-contained frames for SSR/WebSocket) and `RingOpcodeSink` (FFM into
  `libpathland_core`). The wire codec (`com.pathland.view.transport`) mirrors
  `pathland_core_transport` (`PLPL` batch format, self-contained frames + events).

Consistency with `pathland_core::constants` is enforced by the emitter/HTML
tests (golden byte layout + round-trips), replacing the old codegen assert pass.

content.text:
Good catch — let me clarify what that code does and why.

## What the broadcast is for

`CounterApp` is `@ApplicationScoped`: **one shared application instance** with one shared `count`/`name` state. Every time any client mutates that state, the emitter produces a delta frame and `broadcast()` fans it out to **every connected WebSocket** so all browsers stay in sync live (instead of a page reload).

So in the current demo, **application ↔ WebSocket is NOT 1:1** — it's 1 app : N clients, a shared whiteboard. This is deliberate: it mirrors the existing Rust demo `examples/pathland-web`, which also holds a single `count` binding and fans frames to all clients via a `broadcast::Sender<Bytes>`.

## Is that the right model?

It's a choice, not a protocol requirement. Pathland itself is transport-agnostic — the protocol is just opcodes; the **app actor** decides the fan-out. Two valid shapes:

| Model | State | WebSocket | Broadcast |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Shared state** (current) | one app, one `count` | N clients all view it | fan-out to all |
| **Per-session** (1:1) | one app *per connection* | each client has its own | send only to that one client |

The current shared model actually sits a little awkwardly with the "multi-tenant scale-out" goal: there's a single `"counter"` key, so all users collide on one counter. A genuine multi-tenant demo would key state per session/user (e.g. `RedisStateStore` keyed by `connection.id()`).

## Your call

Do you want me to change the demo to a **per-session (1:1)** model — where each WebSocket connection gets its own app instance/counter and deltas go only to that client — or keep the shared-state broadcast (consistent with `examples/pathland-web`)?

I can also do a middle ground: per-session state but still demonstrate cross-client broadcast with an explicit opt-in (e.g. a second "shared board" view), which shows both the 1:1 and the fan-out paths in one demo. Let me know which direction and I'll plan the change.

Understood — per-session 1:1, no fan-out. Let me lay out the plan.

## Per-session architecture

The change moves state out of the single `@ApplicationScoped` bean and into a **per-connection `SessionApp`**. The `Set<WebSocketConnection>` and `broadcast()` disappear entirely; each app instance holds exactly one connection and sends only to it.

### New/removed pieces

**Remove** (in `CounterApp` / demo):
- `Set<WebSocketConnection> clients`, `register()` / `unregister()`, `broadcast(Frame)`.
- The single shared `count`/`name` signals and shared `renderedHtml`/`renderHtml()` join logic.
- `@ApplicationScoped` app-as-state.

**Add**:
- **`SessionApp`** (plain class, per connection) — owns `count`/`name` signals + computeds, `Emitter`, `HtmlRenderer`, and a `FrameOpcodeSink` whose `endFrame` sends the delta straight to its single `WebSocketConnection` (via the already-working `ClientProxy.unwrap` handle). Also owns a `persistEffect` writing to a **session-keyed** `StateStore`.
- **`SessionRegistry`** (`@ApplicationScoped`) — a `Map<String, SessionApp>` + a shared single-threaded executor (serializes all sessions' work; signals stay single-threaded). API: `open(sessionId, connection)`, `dispatch(sessionId, bytes)`, `close(sessionId)`.
- **`PathlandSocket`** → `@WebSocket(path = "/ws/{sessionId}")`, using `connection.pathParam("sessionId")`. On open → `registry.open`; on binary → `registry.dispatch`; on close → `registry.close` (destroys effects + closes the store).
- **`IndexResource`** → renders the **default (stateless)** view + injects `app.js`.

### State keying
`StateStore` keys become `"counter:<sessionId>"` / `"name:<sessionId>"` — this is what makes the same code multi-tenant/scale-out friendly.

### Client (`app.js`)
- Generate a UUID once, persist it in `localStorage`, connect to `ws://host/ws/<uuid>`.
- Delta-hydration + event-send logic stays unchanged.

### Connect flow
`open(sessionId)` → create `SessionApp`, load persisted state from Redis (in-memory fallback), `mount()` — the mount's full frame is emitted through the sink and sent to that one client, so the browser syncs from default SSR to the session's actual state. Subsequent deltas flow 1:1.

Here's the finalized plan.

## Per-session demo (server cookie + per-session SSR)

### 1. `pathland-view` (tiny)
- `InMemoryStateStore` → `ConcurrentHashMap` so SSR (request thread) and sessions (actor thread) can both read state safely. (Redis/Lettuce is already thread-safe.)

### 2. Split the demo app into a registry + per-session actor

**`SessionApp`** (plain class, one per connection) — owns:
- live `count`/`name` `WritableSignal`s + computed labels,
- `Emitter` + `HtmlRenderer` + a `FrameOpcodeSink` whose `endFrame` **sends only to this session's connection** (via the `ClientProxy.unwrap` handle),
- a `persistEffect` writing `count`/`name` to the **session-keyed** stores,
- `dispatch(byte[])` (decode events → run tap action / `name.set`) and `close()` (destroy effects + stores).
- The connection is wired **after** mount, so the mount's full frame is not re-sent (SSR already rendered it); only subsequent deltas flow.

**`PathlandApp`** (`@ApplicationScoped`, replaces `CounterApp`) — the registry:
- shared single-thread executor (serializes all sessions' signal work),
- `Map<String, SessionApp>` keyed by session id,
- `StateStore<Integer>` + `StateStore<String>` (Redis with in-memory fallback), keyed `"counter:<id>"` / `"name:<id>"`,
- `renderHtml(sessionId)` — loads state, builds a **throwaway** view/emitter/render, returns HTML (used by SSR),
- `open(sessionId, connection)` / `dispatch(sessionId, bytes)` / `close(sessionId)`.

A shared `CounterView` builder (view function over the `count`/`name` signals) is reused by both SSR and `SessionApp`.

### 3. `IndexResource`
- `@CookieParam("session") String sessionId`; if absent, generate a UUID and set `Set-Cookie: session=<uuid>; Path=/`.
- Return `app.renderHtml(sessionId)` (per-session persisted state → no flash).

### 4. `PathlandSocket`
- `@WebSocket(path = "/ws")` (unchanged path), read `connection.handshakeRequest().header("Cookie")` → parse `session=`, then `open`/`dispatch`/`close` per session. **No `Set<WebSocketConnection>`, no broadcast.**

### 5. No `app.js` change (cookie is transparent).

### Verification
- `mvn install`; run the packaged jar.
- `curl -i /` returns a `Set-Cookie` header and default HTML; repeat with `-b session=<id>` shows persisted state.
- A WS client with cookie A incrementing does **not** affect cookie B's counter (per-session isolation); reloading with the same cookie restores state from Redis/in-memory.

content.text:
Done. The demo is now strictly 1:1 per-session.

## What changed

- **`SessionApp`** (new) — one app instance per WebSocket connection: its own `count`/`name` signals, emitter, HTML renderer, and a `FrameOpcodeSink` whose `endFrame` sends the delta **only to that single connection**. The connection is wired *after* mount so the initial full frame isn't re-sent (SSR already rendered it).
- **`PathlandApp`** (replaces `CounterApp`) — a registry: `Map<String, SessionApp>`, a shared actor thread, and session-keyed `StateStore`s (`counter:<id>`, `name:<id>`). No `Set<WebSocketConnection>`, no broadcast anywhere.
- **`IndexResource`** — reads the `session` cookie (`@CookieParam`), sets it if absent (`NewCookie`), and renders **that session's** persisted HTML (no flash).
- **`PathlandSocket`** — reads the `session` cookie from the handshake (`connection.handshakeRequest().header("Cookie")`) and routes open/dispatch/close to the session.
- **`InMemoryStateStore`** — now `ConcurrentHashMap` (safe for request-thread SSR + actor-thread writes).
- **`app.js` unchanged** — the cookie is sent by the browser automatically.

## Verified end-to-end

| Session | Action | Result |
|---|---|---|
| A | click ×2 | deltas `Count: 1`, `Count: 2`; SSR `Count: 2` |
| B | click ×1 | delta `Count: 1` (its own, starts at 0); SSR `Count: 1` |
| fresh | none | SSR `Count: 0` |
| A | type "Alice" | deltas `Name: Alice` + field value; SSR `value="Alice"`; B's name stays empty |

Full reactor build green (26 Rust + 26 Java tests). Sessions are isolated, persisted (Redis or in-memory), and deltas flow strictly 1:1 — the broadcast is gone.

The key finding changes everything: **ScopedValue was finalized only in JDK 25 (JEP 506)** — it's still *preview* in JDK 23 and 24. Meanwhile Quarkus 3.17.6 pins **ASM 9.7.1**, which reads class files only up to **Java 23 (major 67)**. These are mutually incompatible:

| `maven.compiler.release` | ScopedValue | Class file | Quarkus dev mode (ASM 9.7.1) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 25 | final | 69 | ❌ `Unsupported class file major version 69` |
| 24 | preview | 68 | ❌ (68 > 67) |
| 23 | preview | 67 | ✅ (but needs `--enable-preview`) |
| 22 | preview | 66 | ✅ (but needs `--enable-preview`) |

So there's no release that gives *both* final ScopedValue *and* Quarkus 3.17.6 dev mode. Let me check whether a newer Quarkus supports Java 25, to weigh the upgrade path.

The picture is now clear. The root cause is a version-lock conflict:

- **ScopedValue is only final in JDK 25** (JEP 506); it's still *preview* in 21–24.
- **Quarkus 3.17.6 pins ASM 9.7.1**, which reads class files only up to Java 23 (major 67).

So `release=25` breaks dev mode (`major version 69`), and `release=22/23/24` makes `ScopedValue` a preview API (your second error). There is no release that gives both final `ScopedValue` *and* Quarkus 3.17.6 dev mode.

Two clean fixes (and one I don't recommend):

**Option A — Upgrade Quarkus (keeps ScopedValue + Java 25).** Latest is 3.39.1; Java-25 support (ASM 9.9+) landed in the 3.18/3.19 era. Bump `quarkus.version` in `lib/java/pom.xml`, keep `maven.compiler.release=25` and `ScopedValue` as-is. `quarkus-websockets-next`/`quarkus-rest` APIs are stable across 3.x, so the demo code should be unchanged. Requires downloading the newer Quarkus (network is available). Docs update to "Java 25".

**Option B — Swap `ScopedValue` → `ThreadLocal` (stays on Quarkus 3.17.6).** Set `maven.compiler.release=22` (FFM is final there; no preview APIs). Replace the `Environment.BUTTON_STYLE` ScopedValue with a `ThreadLocal<ButtonStyle>` set/unset around the scoped render (a `try/finally`).
